cases.source: issue #172 (verbatim; traceback shortened to the library's own frames)
cases.incident:
`engine.plural` raises unexpected `IndexError`

This might be considered invalid input, but `engine.plural` accepts multiple words. When doing so, it can raise an unexpected `IndexError`:

>>> import inflect
>>> engine = inflect.engine()
>>> engine.plural("I'm only here for a minute, John.")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "inflect/__init__.py", line 2403, in plural
    plural = self.postprocess(
  File "inflect/__init__.py", line 2375, in postprocess
    result[index] = result[index].capitalize()
IndexError: list index out of range

This seems to be because `engine.postprocess` expects the `inflected` it's passed to be the same number of words as the `orig` it's passed, but that's not necessarily the case.

one() and only() ignore a custom exception when the exception object is falsy

Passing a custom exception instance as `too_long` (or `too_short`) to `one()` or `only()` normally raises that exception. But if the exception's class defines `__bool__` returning False, the custom exception is discarded and the default ValueError is raised instead. Expected: the custom exception is raised whatever its truthiness.

Deleting a slice from an array corrupts the rendered TOML

After deleting a slice from an Array, the list contents are right but as_string()/dumps() disagree with them:

    import tomlkit
    doc = tomlkit.parse("a = [1, 2, 3]\n")
    del doc["a"][:0]   # deletes nothing
    tomlkit.dumps(doc)  # 'a = []\n'  -- expected 'a = [1, 2, 3]\n'

Other cases: `del arr[-1:]` leaves list(arr) == [1, 2] but renders `[]`; `del arr[:-1]` leaves [3] but the rendering doesn't match either. Expected: the rendered array always matches the list contents.

cases.incident:
match_previous_expr does not handle nested expressions

See this SO post (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78574784/how-to-make-sure-element-has-parsing-precedence-before-other-elements-in-pyparsi), should be able to use match_previous_expr to enforce matching of opening and closing tags. Does not work for nested tags.

fields.Pluck with data_key="" fails to load and dump

A Pluck field whose nested field has `data_key=""` treats the empty key as unset. Loading a valid plucked value raises ValidationError, and dumping it raises KeyError. Ordinary schema fields accept an empty data_key; Pluck should behave the same, for single and many=True nested values.

show_envvar renders sequences and empty envvars badly

With show_envvar=True, the env var hint in error messages and help is wrong for some envvar values:

- envvar="": the error hint shows `(env var: '')` and help shows `[env var: ]`; expected: no hint at all.
- envvar=[]: the error hint shows `(env var: '[]')` and help shows `[env var: ]`; expected: no hint at all.
- envvar=["WEATHER_UNITS", "UNITS"]: the error hint shows `(env var: '['WEATHER_UNITS', 'UNITS']')`; expected: `(env var: 'WEATHER_UNITS', 'UNITS')`.

Empty arbitrary-equality versions are accepted

`Requirement("foo===")` parses without error, and so do `Specifier("===")` and `SpecifierSet("===")`. An arbitrary-equality (===) clause with no version is invalid. Expected: Requirement raises InvalidRequirement, and Specifier/SpecifierSet raise InvalidSpecifier.
